slides.title: Is it true?
slides.text: A claim is something you say is true, like: the plant grows every day. Evidence is the data that backs it up.
slides.alt: The Plant Race case: a chart of a growing plant, and claim cards waiting to be judged against it.

slides.title: Enough data?
slides.text: Two bars are a hunch, not a case. When there is too little data, the honest answer is: we can not tell yet.
slides.alt: The Two Points case: a chart with almost no data in it, where the honest answer is that we can not tell yet.

slides.title: Predict the plant
slides.text: The plant grows 2 cm every day. So day 6 will most likely be 2 cm taller than day 5.
slides.alt: Predict Day 6: the plant chart climbs the same amount every day, so the next bar can be predicted from the pattern.

slides.title: Say only what it shows
slides.text: If Saturday has the tallest bar in a chart of park visitors, the chart supports: most visitors came on Saturday. It does not say why.
slides.alt: The claim card beside the plant chart: each claim must match what the bars actually show, nothing more.

words.means: the data that backs up a claim
use data to say what will happen next

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Data Detective at Clues & Claims and solve 4 cases. Before you pin a claim, ask: does the chart really show it, or can we not tell yet?
slides.alt: The Plant Race case: a chart of a growing plant, and claim cards waiting to be judged against it.
